papers.title: Rotational Perturbation Theory for Magnetic Interactions
papers.abstract: We develop rotational perturbation theory for magnetic interactions in collinear and noncollinear systems, distinguishing prescribed rotations of exchange fields from constrained rotations of magnetic moments. At the full exchange splitting, we derive Green-function expressions for prescribedfield energy curvatures directly from perturbation theory, without invoking the local force theorem; constrained-moment curvatures additionally require the stationary magnetic response and are related to the inverse static susceptibility. We examine noncollinear pair interactions and planar and conical spin spirals, and derive the long-wavelength ferromagnetic spin-wave stiffness and, assuming adiabatic sublattice precession, the antiferromagnetic spin-wave velocity. Orbital-nonlocal magnetic potentials and correlated electronic response reveal further requirements for connecting rotational curvatures to collective magnetic behavior. As a practical extension, we project the complete transverse pair Hessian onto an effective scalar Heisenberg exchange and quantify the unreconstructed curvature. Biquadratic and three-spin examples illustrate why locally extracted exchange coefficients need not represent transferable bilinear interactions.

papers.title: Shortcuts to Adiabaticity via Adaptive Quantum Zeno Measurements
papers.abstract: Stroboscopic measurements of a time-dependent projector generate a quantum Zeno dynamics whose effective Hamiltonian is the Kato-Avron Hamiltonian for parallel transport, which reduces to counterdiabatic driving in the case of a nonselective measurement of the instantaneous eigenprojectors of the system. The same generator arises under continuous monitoring of a time-dependent observable and under a time-varying complex absorbing potential. Departures from the ideal Zeno limit are governed, in all three settings, by a single positive leakage operator with a dynamical and a purely geometric contribution. Matching the corresponding generators yields a model-independent generalized Schulman relation for the quantum Zeno dynamics in the three scenarios, and a purely geometric bound on the measurement resources needed to steer a subspace along a prescribed path.
